lede: Two subjects crowded several feeds at once. Grand Theft Auto VI led Wikipedia with 393,338 views, just 5,050 ahead of the Riemann hypothesis, which also drew 938 points on Hacker News and a wire claim that Claude helped prove it. Little else rose above the usual hum.

throughlines.title: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini
throughlines.gist: A compact open model from Thinking Machines that runs in 5.4 GB of memory, sitting top of HuggingFace and climbing Hacker News, a nudge toward models small enough to run on your own machine.

throughlines.title: Grand Theft Auto VI
throughlines.gist: Rockstar's long-delayed sequel was the day's single biggest draw, leading Wikipedia with 393,338 views while the Grand Theft Auto name also surfaced on Steam's charts.

throughlines.title: Riemann hypothesis
throughlines.gist: A 167-year-old math problem pulled 388,288 Wikipedia views and 938 points on Hacker News for a Lean proof verification, after a wire report that an Anthropic mathematician used Claude to help crack it.
